newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG lashes out against bidder CalEnergy.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG lashes out against bidder CalEnergy.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp. (NYSEG) Friday blasted hostile bidder CalEnergy Co. Inc., saying it thought a recent meeting between the two companies was being held to discuss an existing relationship and not a takeover.

In a letter distributed to NYSEG employees and obtained by Reuters, NYSEG Chairman Wesley von Schack disputed CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol's characterisation of the July 10 meeting in which Sokol discussed a plan to buy NYSEG.

"Clearly, Mr. Sokol came to that meeting with a much different and secret agenda. Prior to that meeting, he in no way signalled to me that he intended to engage in a discussion regarding a possible business combination," von Schack wrote in the letter.

On Tuesday, CalEnergy announced it was launching a $160 million, or $24.50 per share, hostile bid for 9.9 percent of NYSEG in the first part of an acquisition attempt. However, CalEnergy is willing to buy the whole company for $27.50 per share, or $1.9 billion, in a friendly transaction.
CalEnergy quickly defended itself, saying the agenda had been made clear to von Schack. It also noted the meeting is described in its filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
CalEnergy made the hostile approach after it said the NYSEG board rejected its friendly overture. It also has said it still would prefer to negotiate a friendly deal.
NYSEG, based in Binghamton, N.Y., has urged shareholders to take no action until its board makes a recommendation on the bid.

In a statement announcing the bid this week, Sokol said the two executives had discussed a potential price at the meeting and that von Schack had indicated a premium of up to 25 percent might be appropriate. NYSEG's letter to employees did not address any potential pricetag on the company.
Von Schack said he had viewed the meeting as a "preliminary exploratory discussion."
CalEnergy formally launched its tender offer Friday. In the SEC filing, the independent power producer said it bought 241,000, or 0.35 percent, of NYSEG shares between July 1 and July 11.
Shares of NYSEG dipped 6.25 cents to $25.125 on the New York Stock Exchange amid broad market declines. CalEnergy stock was unchanged at $38, also on NYSE.
